teaching.hint: Could the searches for different cells share their expanding frontiers?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Distances from the nearest zero can be computed by starting one breadth-first exploration from every zero simultaneously.
solution_outline.approach: Assign every zero distance zero and put them all into a queue. Expand side-neighbors in breadth-first order, assigning each unvisited neighbor the current distance plus one.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The queue explores distance layers from the entire source set; every assigned cell has its shortest distance to some zero.
solution_outline.correctness: All sources begin at distance zero. Each layer reaches precisely cells one edge beyond earlier layers. A cell first reached at distance d has a length-d route to a zero; a shorter route would have placed it in an earlier layer. Thus every assigned distance is minimal, and connectivity of the rectangular grid guarantees all cells are reached.
solution_outline.complexity: O(mn) time and O(mn) auxiliary space for distances and the frontier.
solution_outline.pitfall: A separate search from each one-cell repeats work; all zeros must seed the same initial frontier.

common_wrong_turns: A separate search from each one-cell repeats work; all zeros must seed the same initial frontier.
source_fidelity_notes: Restated distance without source images and made side adjacency and zero self-distance explicit; introductory simultaneous-source role.
